newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.

text.p: The South African rand was moving crab-like at lower levels toward the end of a dissapointing week late Friday.
The rand was last priced at 4.5535/5565 to the dollar from 4.5495/5425 late Thursday.

The unit faced pressure on a number of fronts over the week as gold softened, other emerging currencies wobbled and a leading investment research firm dubbed South Africa the riskiest bet of the 10 largest emerging markets.
It had just skipped through a key near-term psychological lid of 4.56 rand on Tuesday as offshore banks hoovered up dollars when it hit a wall of liquidity apparently set up by the Reserve Bank.
Dealers said the action left plenty longs searching for a way out of expensive positions, trying to push the unit back to 4.56 by selling into any strength.
The central bank, however refused to to let the rand yield significantly and volumes, as did enthusiasm, waned from Thursday afternoon onward.
That, dealers said, left plently of longs going into the weekend a good thing for the rand's prospects next week.
In cross rate action, lower than expected U.S. PPI data helped the dollar against the crosses and left the rand standing proud against the mark and yen.
It was last fetching 0.3882/3886 marks from 0.3845/3850 marks on Thursday and 24.9835/0110 yen from 24.8215/8599 before.
The rand started firmer against sterling but renewed excitement about Thursday's U.K. rate hike took the wind out of its sails to leave it at 7.7076/7182 from its previous level of 7.6741/6837.
The rands' range for the coming week was pegged beween 4.54 and 4.58 to the dollar
"As long as the Reserve Bank trys to cap the rand, we'll see tight ranges," said one dealer.
In bond dealings, the benchmark R150 loan succumbed to further profit-taking and technical weakness to end the week in the doldrums.
The R150 was last changing hands at 14.315 pct from Thursday's late level of 14.265 pct.
Bond traders said they would be eyeing the rand for direction with stability seen as enough to turn yields south again.
"It's looking a bit oversold here and I think the guys will be happy to take it down again if the rand can keep out of serious trouble," said one.
On the money market, offered rates for three-month NCDs were steady at between 15.65 to 15.70 percent, while the 90-day BA rate was also unchanged at 15.10 percent.
The South African Reserve Bank said the money market shortage jumped to 7.192 billion rand on Thursday from 6.456 billion rand on Wednesday.
Foreigners were net sellers of 746.16 million rand's worth of bonds on Thursday after selling 294.26 million rand's worth on Wednesday, the Bond Exchange said.
Exchange turnover totalled 43.7 billion rand on Thursday, a settlement date.
-- Justin McCamish, Johannesburg newsroom +27 11 482 1003
